summary.button: A button that triggers an action, with five appearances and three sizes.
summary.input: Single-line / multi-line text input, supporting headers, descriptions and password forms.
summary.scroll-view: A container that scrolls, pans and zooms content that overflows the viewport.
summary.icons: WinUI 3 / Fluent System Icons icon components.
summary.checkbox: Select one or more items from a set, with an indeterminate state.
summary.combobox: Pick one option from a list, with text search and an editable mode.

home.heroIntroBefore: A Vue 3 component library referencing the native
home.heroIntroAfter1: controls. It is implemented against real Windows behavior and the matching Windows App SDK source rather than the Fluent Design web specification alone: each control is checked state by state (rest / hover / pressed / selected / focus / disabled) for size, corner radius, stroke, fill and motion, and materials use web approximations of
home.heroIntroAfter2: . Browsers cannot provide every native capability: system-level animations, haptic feedback and native window behaviors are out of scope for a full reproduction, and the implementation distinguishes faithfully reproduced, approximated and unsupported behavior.
home.ctaIntro: Component props, events, examples and API tables are documented on this site; the entries below cover installation, the component inventory and design tokens.
home.metaDescription: A Vue 3 component library referencing the native WinUI 3 controls, implemented against real Windows behavior and the matching Windows App SDK source; sizes, corner radii, strokes, fills and motion are checked state by state, with web approximations for materials such as Mica / Acrylic.

basic.body: Content of tab {index}. Switching tabs unmounts the previous panel, mirroring WinUI, which owns a single ContentPresenter.

close.label: Closable tabs
close.empty: All tabs are closed — press "New tab" to open one
close.hint: The close button and the add button only raise events: removing items and picking the next selection is the consumer’s job. When the selected tab disappears, the component migrates the selection with WinUI’s rule (first enabled tab, wrapping forward).

widthMode.label: Width mode
widthMode.hint: In equal mode every tab is clamp(available / count, 100, 240); compact only collapses unselected tabs — the selected one always restores icon plus text.

overflow.label: Overflowing tab strip
overflow.hint: When space runs out every tab is squeezed to the 100px floor first, then two scroll buttons appear (50 px steps, disabled at either end, continuous scrolling while held). They stay out of the tab order and are hidden from screen readers. No scrollbar is drawn while overflowing (the upstream template has no scrollbar part), so the strip height never changes.

states.label: States and closability
states.overlayLabel: Close buttons only while hovered or selected
states.hint: Hover, pressed, selected and disabled values come straight from TabViewItem’s visual states. Among the overlay modes, Auto and Always behave identically (the same default branch upstream); only on-pointer-over hides the button until hover or selection.
